vocab.notes: na poštu, na nádraží, na koncert
Jdu domů. (But: Jsem doma. I'm at home.)
Soft feminine (like píseň): tramvají = by tram, v tramvaji = in the tram.
Monthly (měsíční) or annual (roční). In Prague it's usually loaded on the Lítačka card or app.

dialogue.setting: Friday afternoon at the office. Eva bumps into her colleague Jakub, who is carrying a big bag.

lines.speaker: Eva
lines.en: Hi, Jakub! Where are you going?

lines.speaker: Jakub
lines.cs: Ahoj! Jdu na [[nádraží|nádraží|acc|after-na-motion]]. Jedu na víkend do [[Olomouce|Olomouc|gen|after-do]].
lines.en: Hi! I'm going to the station. I'm going to Olomouc for the weekend.

lines.speaker: Jakub
lines.cs: Ano, [[vlakem|vlak|ins|means]]. Je to pohodlnější než autobus.
lines.en: Yes, by train. It's more comfortable than the bus.

lines.speaker: Eva
lines.en: And are you walking to the station?

lines.speaker: Jakub
lines.cs: Ne, pojedu [[tramvají|tramvaj|ins|means]]. S tou [[taškou|taška|ins|with-s]] je to daleko.
lines.en: No, I'll take the tram. With this bag it's a long way.

exercises.prompt: Where is Jakub going for the weekend?

hints.explain: Brno would be "do Brna". He says "do Olomouce".
Home would be "domů". He's going "do Olomouce".

exercises.why: "Jedu na víkend do Olomouce." I'm going to Olomouc for the weekend. do + genitive.

exercises.prompt: How will Jakub get to the station?

hints.explain: That's what Eva asked ("pěšky?"). He says no: "pojedu tramvají", I'll go by tram.
By bus would be "autobusem". "Tramvají" is by tram.

exercises.why: "Ne, pojedu tramvají." No, I'll take the tram. Instrumental for the means: tramvají.

lines: Ahoj, jedu na víkend do Olomouce. Jedu vlakem. Jakub

hints.explain: A bus would be "autobusem". "Vlakem" is by train.
On foot is "pěšky". He goes "vlakem", by train.

exercises.why: "Hi, I'm going to Olomouc for the weekend. I'm going by train. Jakub"

exercises.prompt: I'm going to Olomouc for the weekend.
answers: {Jedu na víkend do Olomouce|Na víkend jedu do Olomouce|Jedu do Olomouce na víkend}[.]
exercises.why: See "Word order and the little words": new information goes last, and jsem, se, si, mi, ho… go second.
jet (by vehicle): jedu, jedeš, jede, jedeme, jedete, jedou.

hints.explain: jdeš is from jít (on foot). Travelling by train uses jet: jedeš.

exercises.prompt: I'm going to Brno by train.
exercises.why: Use jet for any journey by vehicle. do takes the genitive (Brno → do Brna), and "by train" is the instrumental: vlakem.

hints.explain: jdu means going on foot. By train, use jet: Jedu.
do takes the genitive: Brno → do Brna.

hints.wrong: Jedu {do Brna s vlakem|s vlakem do Brna}[.]
hints.explain: "By train" is the bare instrumental: vlakem (s vlakem = together with a train).

exercises.why: Means of transport go in the instrumental. Soft feminine nouns ending in a consonant take -í: tramvaj → tramvají.

hints.explain: tramvaj is a soft feminine noun (like píseň), so the instrumental is -í, not -ou: tramvají.

exercises.question: Which case is "poštu"?
exercises.en: I'm going to the post office.
exercises.why: na with movement (where to?) takes the accusative: na poštu. For location (where?) it's the locative: Jsem na poště.
See "Word order and the little words": new information goes last, and jsem, se, si, mi, ho… go second.
do takes the genitive. Neuter -o → -a: kino → do kina.

hints.explain: kino is the nominative. do takes the genitive: do kina.

exercises.why: domů means "(to) home" with movement. It's a fixed word: no preposition.

hints.explain: doma means "at home" (location). For movement towards home, use domů.
do domu means "into the house/building". "Home" is simply domů.
Jedu domů is correct Czech, but it means going home by vehicle. On foot: Jdu domů.

exercises.why: kam = where to. Use it with verbs of motion.

hints.explain: kde means "where" for location. For direction, use kam: Kam jdeš?

options: I go to work by bus. (every day)
I'm going to Brno by train.
answers: I go to work by bus. (every day)

hints.wrong: I'm going to Brno by train.
hints.explain: That one is “Jedu do Brna vlakem.”.

exercises.why: For habits, use the indeterminate verb: jezdit (by vehicle) or chodit (on foot). do práce = to work (genitive).
